evals.prompt: I’m returning to the warehouse handover task after several days. I need enough context to answer the customer’s latest question. Can you catch me up from the task records?
evals.expected_output: Opens with a grouped quick card (Now, Delta, Risks & action), then returns a source-linked full recap with the goal, latest customer question, chronology, decision history, Before/After/Example deltas, problem-attempt-result records, current confidence, and a safe response posture.
assertions: Places the grouped Now, Delta, and Risks & action quick card immediately after any required response header and before full context
Reads each supplied staged path before deciding whether a source gap exists
Names the operator's immediate goal and latest customer question from the staged records
Reconstructs every dated material event, including the latest customer question, with its full date as its own source-labeled timeline entry from durable task records
Lists every literal concrete staged source path on its own full-recap ledger bullet and ends with one safe next posture
States the material Before, After, and Example delta with source-backed scope
Preserves the implementation, verification, and customer-readiness distinction
Ends with one safe response posture without running the task

farplane.title: Task Recap reconstructs a paused ticketed task
farplane.notes: Covers a realistic delayed reply using staged durable sources.

evals.prompt: Before I tell the customer the handover issue is fixed, what do the records actually show?
evals.expected_output: Uses the grouped card to make the conflict between implementation progress and missing runtime proof obvious, avoids a completion claim, and names the concrete evidence or response needed before customer confirmation.
assertions: Places the customer-safe reply in Now and the missing proof in Risks & action
Distinguishes checked ticket work from a passing runtime receipt
Makes the conflicting evidence visible instead of averaging it into a reassuring conclusion
States that customer readiness remains unproven
Names the smallest evidence needed to resolve the conflict
Appends full source-linked details for the proof conflict, listing every concrete staged path on its own ledger bullet and ending with one safe next posture
Does not execute a test or send a customer message

farplane.title: Task Recap rejects an unsupported completion claim
farplane.notes: Regression for stale completion state versus current evidence.

evals.prompt: What have we already tried on the warehouse handover problem, and which paths should we not repeat?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the visible Delta grouped as Before, After, and indented Example; traces each recorded symptom, attempt, observed result, disposition, and remaining impact; preserves the rejected workaround and separates the implemented fix from its unverified runtime outcome.
assertions: Keeps the source-backed Before, After, and indented Example together in Delta
Names the concrete symptom rather than flattening it into a generic bug
Preserves the rejected workaround and the reason it was rejected
Uses a distinct Problems and attempts section to connect each attempt to its observed result, disposition, and remaining impact
Labels each detailed timeline event with its supporting source, retains every literal concrete source path on its own ledger bullet, and ends with one safe next posture
Keeps unresolved runtime verification visible after the implementation attempt
Does not invent an attempt, root cause, or final outcome

farplane.title: Task Recap preserves failed and rejected paths
farplane.notes: Protects the operator from repeating prior work.

evals.prompt: I’m opening an old conversation, but all I remember is that it involved a warehouse handover. Give me the full recap.
evals.expected_output: Returns a bounded grouped source-gap card rather than inventing history, states what cannot be known, and requests a specific ticket, artifact, thread reference, or pasted source needed for a reliable recap.
assertions: Uses Now and Risks & action to make the source gap and needed source scannable
Does not fabricate task details from the topic alone
Explains the limit of an unbound or unavailable task source
Requests the smallest concrete source needed to continue
Avoids creating or mutating a ticket just to manufacture context
Keeps the response useful without claiming a full recap exists

farplane.title: Task Recap exposes a missing durable source

evals.prompt: Please catch me up on the warehouse handover task. The workspace also has an unrelated documentation edit, so keep the recap scoped to this task.
evals.expected_output: Uses the grouped quick card and task records to distinguish relevant implementation state from unrelated documentation changes, labels the snapshot freshness limit, and avoids treating either as completion proof.
assertions: Uses the grouped card to make the relevant Delta and remaining action scannable
Names the task-owned implementation path rather than only calling the worktree scoped
Excludes the unrelated documentation edit from the task delta
Labels the worktree status with its exact capture timestamp and explicitly says it is historical, not live state
Does not let a modified file replace test or review evidence
Returns a safe next action grounded in the task packet

farplane.title: Task Recap excludes unrelated worktree noise
farplane.notes: Protects task boundaries when the checkout is dirty.
